You are working on a VoWLAN design with your customer's wired networking team. How many distinct priority levels do you expect for the voice applications?
1 priority level, but 2 queues (one for uplink traffic, one for downlink traffic)
1 priority level per client and AP pair, so the total number depends on the expected number of clients
1 priority level for voice RTP, 1 priority level for voice control and RTCP
1 priority level for VoWLAN client traffic, 1 priority level for wired VoIP client traffic
C
Voice RTP media and voice control/RTCP traffic may be assigned distinct priority levels so real-time media and its control traffic receive appropriate QoS treatment.

ABC Company has a WLAN controller with 10 controller-based APs; the Voice SSID is configured for centralized data forwarding. Each AP is connected to an access port on a layer-2 Ethernet switch. Each layer-2 switch is uplinked to a single layer-3 core Ethernet switch. The WLAN controller is connected directly to the layer-3 core Ethernet switch. Layer-3 tunnels are created between all controller-based APs and the WLAN controller. A voice server is connected to the layer-3 Ethernet switch. When a voice-enabled QoS STA sends an IP data packet to a voice server in this scenario, the DSCP value carried in the STA's IP data packet gets mapped to what and by which device?
The DSCP value is mapped to an IEEE 802.1Q priority tag value by the WLAN controller.
The DSCP value is mapped to the DSCP value in the encapsulating IP header by the layer-3 switch.
The DSCP value is mapped to an IEEE 802.1p (802.1D-2004) UP value by the access point.
The DSCP value is mapped to an IEEE 802.1Q VLAN tag by the access point.
A
With centralized forwarding, the WLAN controller handles the decapsulation and wired-side QoS mapping. The received DSCP marking is mapped to the 802.1Q priority tag on the controller's egress path.

Given: For this fill-in the blank question, each answer option contains an answer for the first and second blanks, separated by a dash "”". Choose the answer option that correctly fills in both blanks in the following sentence. A WLAN may use 802.11 admission control to ________, and admission control requirements are configured separately for each ________.
Block stations with inadequate security parameters ” SSID
Identify voice-enabled wireless devices ” AP radio (that is, 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz)
Regulate the available bandwidth resources ” Access Category
Mark ingress and egress frames with priority values ” TCP/IP port
C
802.11 admission control reserves or regulates available airtime/bandwidth resources. The admission-control requirement is configured per WMM access category.
In a large enterprise (5000+ wireless users), by what would NOT be a recommended method by which IP addresses and VLANs are assigned to different clients associated to the same AP?
Each SSID is mapped to a static VLAN assignment
Upstream AAA servers dynamically assign VLANs to each user or group profile
Radio signal metrics (RSSI, SNR, etc.) of WLAN clients are triangulated for location-based VLAN assignment during association
Multiple VLAN pools are designated for an SSID and user IP addresses are selected in a roundrobin fashion from the associated pools
C
RSSI is an indirect signal-strength measurement. Multipath, reflections, device orientation, and hardware differences make it less precise for location than timing- or angle-based methods.
In a multiple channel architecture (MCA) network supporting 802.1X authentication, what aspect of WLAN design affects client roaming efficiency and effectiveness?
PHY standard used by the AP
Key caching protocols
Cipher suite
PHY standard used by client
B
PMK caching lets a client reuse previously established key material when returning to an AP, reducing the time and authentication work required to roam.

An associated STA detects a new BSS with the same SSID as the STA's current BSS. The new BSS uses a different IP subnet than the current BSS. If the STA is configured to use 802.1X/EAP preauthentication, what is likely to occur?
The STA will not attempt to preauthenticate because the new BSS uses a different IP subnet.
The STA will attempt to preauthenticate, but fail because the new BSS uses a different data-link broadcast domain.
The STA will attempt to preauthenticate and succeed if DHCP is supported on the new subnet.
The STA will attempt to preauthenticate and succeed if IP Mobility is enabled on the AP or WLAN controller.
B
802.1X preauthentication depends on Layer 2 reachability to the target BSS. A different data-link broadcast domain prevents the preauthentication exchange from succeeding in this scenario.

Given: A WLAN controller is connected to ABC Company's core layer 3 Ethernet switch with an IEEE 802.1Q trunk connection. The WLAN controller's native VLAN is VLAN 6 and its IP address is 10.0.14.2 . Lightweight APs supporting centralized forwarding are connected to the network on VLANs 7, 8, and 9, and they each build a Layer 3 tunnel back to the WLAN controller's IP address. The dynamically assigned IP addresses received by each AP from a DHCP server will be ________________.
Associated with the VLAN on which they are connected.
Associated with the native VLAN of the WLAN controller.
Associated with VLAN 1, the default VLAN for new APs
Associated with a non-routable VLAN until the MAC address of the AP is removed from the controller's MAC filter
A
An AP's DHCP address belongs to the VLAN on which its switch port places it. The controller's native VLAN does not automatically determine the AP's address subnet.
What is the purpose of DHCP Option 43, and how is it used with WLANs?
It provides clients with a temporary IP address on a restricted VLAN until 802.1X authentication is completed. Then the client receives its long-term IP address.

It provides IP address bindings for specific network nodes that require long-term IP address assignments. WLAN controllers are configured to use Option 43 to receive long-term IP address leases that are centrally managed with DHCP.
It supports vendor-specific IP address attributes for node discovery purposes. APs use Option 43 with vendor class identifiers to obtain the IP address of a centralized WLAN controller.
It integrates a DHCP server with AAA servers and user databases to dynamically assign IP addresses to client devices. During 802.1X, the AAA server uses
C
DHCP Option 43 carries vendor-specific discovery information. APs use it, together with vendor class information, to learn the address of a WLAN controller.

You deployed an AP and installed its antenna, and you now need to set the AP transmit power. Given a desired EIRP of 21 dBm, and an antenna gain of 5.85 dBd connected through 25 feet of cable with a loss specification of 4 dB feet. Assuming that there is no significant loss from the connectors, what should be the transmit power level for this AP?
10 mW
14 mW
20 mW
25 mW
D
A 5.85 dBd antenna is approximately 8 dBi. Subtracting the 1 dB cable loss from the 21 dBm EIRP target leaves about 14 dBm transmitter output, or approximately 25 mW.
What kind of antenna results in a nearly circular pattern on the azimuth chart but a very flat donut shape on the elevation chart?
High gain omni-directional
20 degree vertical yagi
120 degree horizontal sector
60 degree horizontal patch
B
A vertical Yagi has a narrow elevation beam and a nearly circular azimuth pattern. This produces a flat, donut-like elevation pattern while radiating around the horizontal plane.
What is a radome?
A type of semi-circular ceiling found in atriums and that is a heavy cause of RF reflection.
A weatherproof piece of plastic covering an antenna or antenna system.
The unit used to measure the signal reflected backward by the end of a cable.
A piece of metal positioned behind APs mounted on outdoor poles, designed to limit the butterfly effect.
B
A radome is a weather-resistant, typically nonconductive cover over an antenna or antenna system. It protects the antenna without acting as a metal RF shield.
Of the following antenna connector types, which one is the smallest?
RP-TNC
MC Connector
N Connector
Male N Connector
A

The supplied answer key identifies RP-TNC. Connector-size comparisons can be easy to confuse with other miniature RF connectors, so verify this item against the diagram or source reference before relying on it.
You are creating an outdoor bridge link that spans more than 1000 yards. Which one of the following antenna types is more likely to be included in the design?
Yagi
Omni
Patch
Panel
A
A Yagi is a directional antenna with useful gain for a long point-to-point path. Its focused pattern helps concentrate energy toward the remote endpoint.
What is the purpose of Friis transmission equation [ (LdB) = 20 log(d) + 20 log (f) - 27.55 ]?
Calculate earth bulge to determine minimum antenna height
Calculate receive sensitivity for an 802.11 radio/antenna pair
Calculate RF path loss in free space
Calculate the loss experienced between the intentional radiator and antenna
C
The Friis free-space path-loss equation estimates the attenuation between two antennas in unobstructed free space as a function of distance and frequency.
Why does a frame transmitted at 1 Mbps have a greater usable range than the same frame transmitted at 54 Mbps?
Free space path loss causes greater signal dispersion for higher rate transmissions.
Receiver sensitivity requirements are lower for frames transmitted with less complex modulation and coding.
To improve reliability, 802.11 STAs increase transmit power as the signaling rate decreases.
Lower data rate RF transmissions travel at higher speeds and are less likely to experience collisions.
B
Lower PHY rates use simpler modulation and coding and therefore require less signal strength at the receiver. That improved receiver sensitivity allows the frame to be decoded at a greater distance.
What basic RF math formula should be used as a baseline to convert an RF value in units of dBm into a value of mW? *Note: "dBm" in the formulas represents the known dBm value
0 dBm = 1 mW
mW C.
mW mW
A
0 dBm equals 1 mW. This is the reference point used to convert between logarithmic dBm values and linear milliwatts.

Given: You are evaluating the theoretical and real-world RF gain benefits of transmit and receive features introduced by 802.11 with MIMO. This exercise allows you to quantify the features value in a real-world environment. What is the maximum theoretical signal gain of chip-based TxBF and MRC (as features) when compared to the same AP using only a single antenna for transmit and receive (effectively simulating a 1x1 chip)?
2 Rx or Tx chains = 3 dBi gain 3 Rx or Tx chains = approx 5 dBi gain 4 Rx or Tx chains = 6 dBi gain
2 Rx or Tx chains = 1 dBi gain 3 Rx or Tx chains = 2 dBi gain 4 Rx or Tx chains = 3 dBi gain
2 Rx or Tx chains = 3 dBi gain 3 Rx or Tx chains = 6 dBi gain 4 Rx or Tx chains = 9 dBi gain
2 Rx or Tx chains = approx 4-6.5 dBi gain 3 Rx or Tx chains = approx 7-10 dBi gain
D

Transmit beamforming focuses energy toward the intended client, while MRC combines signals from multiple receive chains. Theoretical gain increases with the number of chains, but actual gain depends on channel conditions, antenna spacing, and feedback.

Given: In your regulatory domain, a Tx Power Level of "1" is equivalent to 17 dBm. For every integer increment (e.g. from 1 to 2) to the Tx Power Level, the APs transmit power is halved. In units of mW, what is the actual transmit power for an AP configured at a Tx Power Level of "4"?
50 mW
8 mW
C

The stated rule halves power at each level: 17 dBm is about 50 mW at level 1, then 25 mW, 12.5 mW, and 6.25 mW at level 4. The supplied key says 12.5 mW, which appears inconsistent with the stated three halvings.

You told your customer that multipath fading may be mitigated simply by moving one or both of the receivers antennas a small amount, usually by one to four wavelengths away from its original position. Your customer is prepared to make the change, but does not know the wavelength for 802.11ac. What is the approximate wavelength of an 802.11ac radio wave?
5.5 cm (2.16 inches)
12 cm (4.72 inches)
15.24 cm (6 inches)
45 cm (17.71 inches)
A
At roughly 5 GHz, wavelength is about 6 cm; 5.5 cm is the closest listed approximation. Moving an antenna by a fraction or multiple of a wavelength can change multipath fading.
What is a valid 40 MHz channel configuration in the 2.4 GHz ISM band where channels 1-11 are permitted?
4 (primary), +1 (secondary)
2 (primary), -1 (secondary)
8 (primary), +1 (secondary)
1 (primary), 6 (secondary)
A
A 40 MHz channel is formed from a primary channel and its paired secondary channel. The listed primary/secondary arrangement is the valid pair under the stated 2.4 GHz channel plan.
